summary: Official information for UI/UX brief 2, plus the satellite chip. I5: web/src/official/hooks.ts exports useOfficialAtPoint(lon, lat), useOfficialNow() and useOfficialBadge(). They give explicit states that are never an all-clear: 'none listed' only where Cal OES or NWS was really checked; 'not checked', 'past date' and 'unavailable' each with a reason. Each result keeps the issuer, its own times, a link and a caveat. The components are ui/feed/OfficialNow.tsx (compact rows with 'More'; a California variant on the overview) and extras/ImageryChip.tsx (the newest image, shown with one click; a compact caption placed by measurement next to the chip). I6: official/mapLayer.ts mountOfficialLayers draws NWS fire weather outlines (the open fire's alerts, archived for replays, or California's on the overview) and the highlight of a selected official row. Its legend entry and credit flow through extras/runtime, so MapLegend and MapAttribution needed no change. U-R1: evacuation rows are timed by the issuer, else by Cal OES's copy or layer time, never by the fetch time. They carry the issuer, the distance to the fire, and 'Cal OES does not say which fire this is for' outside the analysis area. zonesAtPoint respects the queried bbox, and the camera summary uses Cal OES's list time. U-R2: FeedItem gains url, issuer, issuedMs, updatedMs, expiresMs, checkedMs, bounds, status, distanceKm, highlight, links, sections, archived, notes, timeNotGiven and children; details show 'Issued by', the issuer's times, 'Open source', 'Checked by Fire-3d' and the verbatim text on demand. U-R6: CAL FIRE change rows read like 'CAL FIRE: 50 % contained (was 25 %)' (a real change on Norte), plus a final-record row for past fires with the note that the history is not available. U-R7: NWS rows keep the verbatim event, 'until' and headline, show every segment's text on demand, stay listed 48 h as 'Expired' and carry an archived label for replays. U-R5: official rows fit and highlight their area and seek only inside the observed record; live rows are never dimmed 'later'. U-R8: new kind meaning, empty-feed wording and a live quiet-period row. U-R10: filters 'Official · All · Key events', a day's satellite passes in one row, and the time zone in Public. O-R15: the chip and caption, a newest-first image list (true color first, US spelling) and compact legend entries with platform and time. C-R8: plain words in Public ('model re-run on past weather'), no run ids in the Public feed, '+ Note' in Command only. U-R11 (P2): kind glyphs with an automated dot on Forensic Key Events. Decision 10 (zooming changes the open fire): one shared per-URL query cache (instant re-focus, shared requests, unused requests aborted), incident guards on every reader, and time-dependent queries that wait for the new fire's own timeline. Also fixed location's bug report: the NOW marker is quantised like the timeline, so a live fire at hh:mm:41 is no longer shown as a past date.
verification:
Gates (final run): cd web && npm run typecheck gave 0 errors. npm run lint gave 55 warnings, the baseline: all in src/scene, 0 elsewhere. npm test passed 671/671 tests in 55 files; my areas (src/official, src/extras, src/ui/feed, src/ui/timeline) have 187 tests in 24 files. npm run build succeeded. cd backend && uv run pytest -q: 597 passed. The unit tests use fixtures recorded from the real API: Eaton's IEM archive answer, Cooley's live quiet answer, the backend's live LOX Red Flag Warning CAP sample (two segments) and CAL FIRE for Eaton and Henderson. In the app (API 8715 with FIRE3D_LIVE=0, Vite 5184, Playwright with GPU Chrome, built fires only, no builds triggered):
- Henderson (live), Official now: 'Evacuation Order · 1 zone · Orange County', '14 mi from the fire · Cal OES does not say which fire this is for', 'Listed by Cal OES Oct 17, 18:01 PDT (no issuer time)'. CAL FIRE: '3,160 acres · 65 % contained · active, Updated by CAL FIRE Oct 18, 08:01 PDT'. NWS: 'No Red Flag Warning or Fire Weather Watch in effect near this fire. Not an all-clear.'
- Cooley: quiet states, 'None listed within 15 km of this fire. Not an all-clear: follow local officials.'
- Eaton replay at Jan 8, 2025 12:00 PST: evacuations 'not available for past dates'. CAL FIRE final record 14,021 acres, 100 %, edited Aug 6, 2026, with the lagged-edit note. Archived Red Flag Warning LOX FW.W #1 'until Jan 10, 14:48 PST' and Fire Weather Watch 'from Jan 9, 18:00 PST (end time unclear in the archive)'. The outlines are on the map, with the 'Fire weather alert (NWS)' legend entry and the credit 'Fire weather alerts: National Weather Service via Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive'. 'Show area' fits and highlights the warning's zones.
- Norte: the real CAL FIRE change row 'CAL FIRE: 50 % contained (was 25 %)' at 10:25 PDT, checked separately. At its NOW marker 00:42:41Z, opened by link and by zoom focus, Official now lists the Evacuation Order, not 'past date'.
- Fire switching (Henderson to Cooley to Norte, 60 ms apart): never a previous fire's rows ('Checking Cal OES…' instead). Re-focusing Henderson showed its data at once with 0 requests; unused requests were aborted.
- Feed: 'Official 1 · All 11 · Key events 6'; times shown as '21:18 PDT'; the quiet row 'No new heat seen by satellites since Oct 16, 14:48 PDT'; 'Satellite passes on Oct 16: 5'; the Red Flag Warning details show the issuer, Issued and Until times, the verbatim parts and 'Checked by Fire-3d'.
- Satellite chip on Cooley: 'Satellite · newest 20 h ago · 375 m · VIIRS NOAA-21'. One click shows the image; the caption ('not live', time, age, pixels, cloud cover) is placed without covering any chrome.
- Phone sheets at 390x844 fit the screen; the 'Updates' badge shows 2 on Eaton (fire weather) and 1 on Henderson (order).
- Forensic Key Events show the kind glyphs. No page errors in any run.
contract_deviations: I5 evacuation.zones[].distanceKm is number | null (null when the fire's position is not known).
I5 fireWeather.alerts[].url is string | null (https only), and headline is '' when NWS gives none.

I5 fireWeather has no 'not-checked' state. A point outside the open fire's checked area uses the statewide NWS answer at the current time; past times outside it are 'past-date'; points outside California are 'unavailable' with reasonCode 'not_checked'.

I5 results carry additive fields: evacuation reason, links, bounds, layerOff, listedMs, outsideAnalysisArea, group, name, message; fireWeather archived, credit, sourceUrl, reasonCode, reason, caveat and alert phase, timeText, sentMs, coversReportedLocation, nearestKm, ugcs, bounds; calfire final, agencies, checkedMs, recordingSinceMs, containedMs, reason, caveats.
I5 useOfficialBadge() returns { count: 0, level: null } on the overview: the badge is about the open fire.
I6 mountOfficialLayers also returns layerIds(); update(state) accepts { visible: boolean } (hide or show everything) and otherwise re-syncs.

CONTRACT 12.3: ExtrasSync now fetches Cal OES zones whatever the evacuation toggle says (the toggle hides them on the map, legend and credits only), and fetches the imagery list for the chip while the imagery layer is off (one list per fire).
ExtrasLayerKey gains 'fireWeather', which is not a MapLayerKey; EXTRAS_LAYER_KEYS includes it. ExtrasLegendEntry gains an optional compact label; LegendSwatch gains kind 'outline'.
FeedFilter gains 'official'; FeedTopic gains 'calfire' | 'fire-weather' | 'quiet'; FeedInput gains preset, groupPasses and wallMs.
zonesAtPoint returns [] outside the response bbox; evacuationAtPoint tells 'not checked' from 'none listed'. The camera summary is timed by Cal OES's list time.
All extras and official queries share one per-URL cache (extras/jsonQuery.ts) instead of per-hook state; the state shape (data, loading, error, refresh) is unchanged.
known_issues: No live Red Flag Warning or Fire Weather Watch was in effect in California during the build. Live outlines and rows are covered by unit tests on the recorded live CAP sample; on screen they were checked with Eaton's archived warning.
The shell's chip slot is 300 px (--m-chip-w). The chip always keeps 'newest <age> · <pixel size>'; the platform and clock time give way first and are in the tooltip, the caption and the legend.

Decision 10's zoom focus also reacts to fits requested by official rows. Fitting Henderson's Orange County zone (14 mi away) focuses the Norte Fire it touches; the selected row stays and reads 'touches the fire area'.
Highlighted NWS zones show the interior boundaries between adjacent fire weather zones (no client-side dissolve).
The IEM archive can list a watch's end before its onset; such alerts read '(end time unclear in the archive)' and use the archive's phase.
For live alerts that left the NWS feed before this page loaded, the 48 h 'Expired' listing depends on the backend keeping ended alerts; the session memory covers alerts seen while the page is open.
notes_for_integrator: 1. The OfficialNow California variant (statewide NWS alerts plus 'zoom in on a fire or pick one') is ready, but the shell's overview panel does not mount it; mounting <OfficialNow /> there is optional. 2. Decision 10: if official fits should not change the open fire, the map's zoom focus could skip camera moves started by official rows. fitOfficialBounds in web/src/official/select.ts is the single call site and can pass a flag once MapFlyTo has one (state/workspace.ts belongs to shell). 3. Consider widening --m-chip-w to about 380 px on desktop so the chip shows the platform. 4. LayersPanel still renders ImageryPanel under the recent-imagery toggle, a second copy of the chip's list (harmless). 5. lib/plainLanguage.ts (location's) forecastDescription still titles replay runs 'Hindcast (72 h)'. My timeline overrides it in Public; other Public readers of forecastDescription (Analysis drawer, card details) may still say 'hindcast'. 6. map/mapController.ts mounts mountOfficialLayers after bindExtrasLayers with beforeId [EVAC_LAYERS.tint, ...draped] and topBeforeId topLayers(), as documented; keep that order. 7. Dev handle: window.__officialRuntime (calfire, fireWeather, statewide, seen, highlight). 8. The satellite caption is portaled to document.body (z-index 25) and placed next to the chip avoiding every [data-chrome] element, so new floating chrome needs only its data-chrome attribute.
